active_themes.label: AI Spending Backlash
active_themes.summary: The Nasdaq closed at 23,586, down 0.62% and well under Monday's 24,090 peak but still above the 22,618 low. S&P Global Ratings warned it could cut Nvidia's credit rating by one notch over rising management and governance risk, adding a new overhang on top of the unresolved accounting probe. The open question is whether the Nasdaq holds above 22,618 without fresh Nvidia-specific good news.

active_themes.label: Gulf Oil Slowly Returns
active_themes.summary: Brent rose 3.51% to $94.61 and WTI 1.99% to $83.68 after mine strikes on ships revived supply worries, extending the bounce driven by threats to Saudi output. Brent is now just under $95, so the market still prices a risk premium, not lost barrels. The open question is whether a confirmed outage pushes prices decisively through that level.

active_themes.label: Global Borrowing Costs Climb
active_themes.summary: The 10-year yield fell to 4.85% and the 30-year to 5.24%, each down 0.06 points, on a day of hot inflation. Bonds are being bought as protection, not sold on inflation fear. The open question is whether yields turn back up toward 5.25% once the growth scare fades, or stay pinned lower by recession worries.

active_themes.label: Fed Eyes Another Hike
active_themes.summary: The PCE inflation gauge rose to 3.8% year over year in October, its highest since May and above forecasts, which all but locks in a hike at the Fed's decision early next month. Waller's half-point idea is still unechoed by any other policymaker. Long-term yields fell on the print, so the bond market is pricing growth damage ahead of inflation. The open question is whether stocks and bonds start pricing a string of hikes.

active_themes.label: New 20% Tariff Round
active_themes.summary: The administration announced new 20% tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China, Japan and the EU, after an eight-month trade investigation. Tariffs raise import costs just as inflation re-accelerates, which narrows the Fed's room to ease. The open question is whether trading partners retaliate and how much of the cost lands on consumers.

active_themes.label: Forced Selling Everywhere
active_themes.summary: Gold fell 2.45% to $3,561.90 today, giving back about two-thirds of Monday's bounce from the $3,515.40 low of 2026-11-20. It fell on a day the dollar slipped and yields were flat, so neither explains it, and the likeliest reading is continued cash-raising by investors hurt in tech. Gold and the Nasdaq falling together again keeps the liquidation story alive. A close under the $3,515.40 low would erase the bounce entirely.

open_watchlist.meaning: The AI-drives-rates argument would have bond-market confirmation, which is the sharpest pressure on high-priced tech shares.
Demand for AI stock itself would be fading, so the IPO stops being a side effect and becomes a signal.
The AI sell-off is extending past Friday's drop, which would mean the funding doubt is deepening and not stabilizing.
Fear of economic damage is overpowering the inflation worry, which would make a Fed hike harder to justify and mean the market expects pain from the AI unwind.
A drop of about 9% from today's $165.05 close would show the CEO-return relief is fading while the accounting probe still hangs over the stock.
That would take gold under its prior session's forced-selling low and show the cash-raising phase is resuming rather than ending.
Oil is pricing actual supply loss from the Houthi threats, not just a risk premium, which adds to inflation pressure ahead of Fed decisions.
The quiet rotation has turned into a renewed panic, which would bring back forced selling across assets.

open_watchlist.condition: S&P Global Ratings cuts Nvidia's credit rating by one notch.
open_watchlist.meaning: The governance concerns would become a formal downgrade, extending the overhang on the AI leader.

open_watchlist.condition: Brent crude closes above $95 a barrel.
open_watchlist.meaning: The oil move would be more than a risk premium, adding another inflation push just as the Fed prepares to hike.
